title: Georgia's 4th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The general election for Georgia's 4th Congressional District will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a representative to the U.S. House. Incumbent Democratic Rep. Hank Johnson, first elected in 2006, is seeking an 11th term after defeating two primary challengers in May 2026. He will face Republican nominee James "Jim" Duffie, a real estate broker and businessman who won the GOP primary unopposed. The district, covering parts of DeKalb and Gwinnett counties in Atlanta's eastern suburbs, is heavily Democratic and has not elected a Republican since its current boundaries were drawn after the 1990 census.
polling_note: No publicly available opinion polls were found for this race as of June 2026. The district is considered safely Democratic.

candidates.name: Hank Johnson
candidates.summary: Henry C. "Hank" Johnson Jr. has represented Georgia's 4th Congressional District since 2007. He is a senior member of the House Judiciary Committee and ranking member of its Subcommittee on Courts, Intellectual Property, Artificial Intelligence, and the Internet. Johnson has focused on court reform, civil rights, consumer protections, and has helped secure over $5 billion in federal investments for Georgia.

candidates.name: James Duffie
candidates.summary: James R. "Jim" Duffie is a real estate broker and businessman who won the Republican nomination for Georgia's 4th Congressional District unopposed in the May 2026 primary. A Georgia Tech graduate and U.S. Navy veteran who served aboard the nuclear submarine USS Skate, he has owned multiple real estate companies and served as founder and CEO of ABLE Foundation Corporation. Duffie previously ran for the Georgia House of Representatives in 2016 and has been active with the Georgia for FairTax organization.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for this race, limiting confidence to medium. However, district fundamentals are extremely clear: Hank Johnson is a long-serving 10-term Democratic incumbent first elected in 2006; the district (parts of DeKalb and Gwinnett counties) is described as heavily Democratic; and no Republican has won this seat under its current post-1990-census boundaries. Johnson defeated two primary challengers in May 2026 and faces Republican nominee Jim Duffie, a real estate broker and Navy veteran who won his primary unopposed. While Duffie is a credible candidate, the district's partisan lean and Johnson's incumbency make a Democratic victory overwhelmingly likely, consistent with a safe-D rating (95%+ party win probability).
